mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses discount rates for equity cash flows, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days as the market prices in lower future financing costs.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns show no significant positive correlation with FEDFUNDS declines (Rank IC < 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals aggressive monetary tightening that immediately suppresses equity valuations through higher discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in < 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in employment (PAYEMS) and declining unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a labor market tightening that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days through joint economic momentum.
failure_condition: The joint signal (PAYEMS rising + UNRATE falling) fails to generate positive 20-day returns in > 50% of cases (Rank IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In early economic expansion, housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 1300 units and strong consumer spending (RSAFS) above 700,000 million dollars signal robust demand growth that elevates corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST > 1300 and RSAFS > 700000 (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A declining unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates tightening labor market conditions that support sustained consumer spending and corporate profit growth, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days through consistent economic momentum.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns show no significant positive correlation with UNRATE declines (Rank IC < 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Accelerating inflation (CPIAUCSL > 300) triggers immediate market concerns about aggressive Fed policy, compressing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in < 40% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 300 (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent expansion in industrial production (INDPRO) and GDP (GDPC1) signals robust supply chain resilience and economic growth, supporting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days through sustained output momentum.
failure_condition: The joint signal (INDPRO rising + GDPC1 rising) fails to produce positive 60-day returns in > 50% of cases (Rank IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Housing market contraction (HOUST < 1200 units) during late-cycle economic phases dampens consumer confidence and spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days through demand weakness.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when HOUST < 1200 (t-test p > 0.05).
